Quick triage notes from the runtime team (short):
- Observed: two pools showing saturation concurrently: hosted-us-east-infer (GPU util 97–99%) and dedicated-west-pool-3 (GPU util 95–99%).
- Autoscaler behaviour: provisioning lag of ~9–12 minutes for new GPU nodes during this spike; pending queue depth jumped from ~420 -> ~1,200 in 8 minutes.
- Effect: queued requests hit our retry window; many clients retry aggressively (default 3x), creating retry amplification and a transient 5xx avalanche.

Immediate mitigations we can run now (order matters):
1) Activate emergency burst: add +4 burst GPUs to dedicated-west-pool-3 and bump hosted pool burst capacity (requires temporary billing override).
2) Route the Galenetics primary route to fallback-model-small-quant (CPU-friendly) to shed GPU pressure — expect ~40% longer latency but dramatic reduction in GPU memory pressure.
3) Deploy temporary client-facing retry policy: reduce client retries to 1 and extend client timeout to avoid tight retry loops. We can push a routing header so only Galenetics traffic is affected.
4) Pre-warm the added nodes and force KV-cache priming for the route.

I attached the autoscaler snapshot (autoscaler-metrics.png) showing the spike pattern. If we can't get burst capacity immediately, the safer short-term path is (2) + (3) above.

Ask: Authorization to start emergency burst and to change routing policies. Also need ops contact at Galenetics to coordinate the fallback cutover window (we recommend immediate cutover, can be done in ~4 minutes).
